judged_text: The webhook implements create-or-update as a findFirst followed by create/update with no transaction and no unique constraint on Credential(userId, appId), so two concurrent deliveries for the same user+app both miss in findFirst and both execute create. Duplicate (userId, appId) credential rows are created — the codebase's own createOAuthAppCredential uses deleteMany-before-create precisely because no unique index exists — after which app-credential lookups return ambiguous rows, and the webhook's findFirst (no orderBy) updates an arbitrary one of the duplicates while a stale sibling keeps serving bookings; webhook delivery semantics make concurrent retries the normal case, not an edge case.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the create-or-update logic is implemented as `findFirst` followed by either `credential.update` or `credential.create`, with no transaction/locking and no `upsert`. This is a real, diff-grounded race condition pattern: concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no row” and both attempt `create`. However, the finding’s stronger claim (that duplicates will definitely be created because there is no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`) cannot be verified from this diff since the Prisma schema/DB constraints are not shown here. So the concurrency concern is valid, but whether it manifests as duplicate rows vs. a unique-constraint error is not provable from the provided changes.
